The solution is complete and fully verified. Here is the summary.

## Deliverable

`/home/kara/fencelock/` — a self-contained Go 1.26 module (`fencelock`) implementing the lease-based distributed mutex, plus `SOLUTION.md` (the markdown deliverable with root-cause analysis, exact code, and verification).

### Files
| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `coordinator.go` | Single grant authority; fencing **token incremented on every grant, not on renewal**; atomic `Acquire` (so duplicate/concurrent grants mint exactly one token) |
| `holder.go` | Renewal loop with **jittered exponential backoff** and **monotonic-time expiry**; local lease shortened by `MaxClockSkew` so it can never outlive the coordinator fence |
| `resource.go` | **Fenced resource** — rejects any write with `token <= lastAccepted`, the hard mutual-exclusion guarantee |
| `clock.go` | Injectable clock (deterministic virtual clock in tests, monotonic `time.Now` in prod) |
| `sim_test.go` / `stress_test.go` | Verification suite |
| `SOLUTION.md` | Problem statement, root-cause analysis, full code, verification |

### Key decisions that satisfy the spec
- **Fencing token** guarantees exclusion even under split-brain/skew/duplicate grants — leases alone cannot.
- **Monotonic time** for all expiry checks; local lease reduced by 250 ms skew allowance.
- **Jittered exponential backoff** in renewal + defensive give-up before `MinRenewLead`, so a ≤2 s partition never costs the lock while a live lock is protected.
- **Lease ≫ skew** (the subtle bug the stress test caught: sizing lease ≈ skew made holders unable to hold).

### Verification (all pass under `-race`, stable across repeated runs)
```
--- PASS: TestConcurrentAcquireSingleWinnerPerGrant
--- PASS: TestSequentialAcquireAndStaleRenew
--- PASS: TestHolderRefusesWriteAfterMonotonicExpiry
--- PASS: TestSkewRespected
--- PASS: TestHolderSurvivesTwoSecondPartition
--- PASS: TestStressMutualExclusion   # 50 seeds × 5 holders, injected skew/partitions/duplicates
PASS
ok  	fencelock	2.069s
```

The stress test constructed 50 adversarial schedules and asserted that every accepted write's fencing token is strictly increasing — i.e., no two holders ever mutated the resource under any injected schedule.

signatures.description: Implement a lease-based distributed mutex where the holder must renew before expiry or lose the lock, tolerating clock drift up to 250ms between nodes and partitions up to 2s without any fencing violation (two holders ever overlapping). The renewal loop must use jittered backoff, monotonic time for expiry checks, and a fencing-token counter incremented on every grant so stale holders writes are rejected by the resource. The grader injects pauses, clock skew, and duplicate grant messages and asserts mutual exclusion under every schedule.
